sources.title: DHARMA: Pallava Epigraphy corpus
sources.note: Scholarly project description, read through the indexed original. Approximately 550 inscriptions associated with Pallava rule in South India, fourth to ninth centuries. Used for broad chronology; imported intervals and decoded geometry are separately documented in identities.json.

sources.title: Emmanuel Francis: Mandagapattu inscription of Vicitracitta, DHARMA INSPallava00027
sources.note: Edition revised from autopsy and photographs; Sanskrit foundation verse, approximately 600 to 625. Original Grantha writing is represented here by its published scholarly Roman transliteration. The unambiguous word aniṣṭakam occurs in line 1; Brocquet’s French translation renders it sans briques. Direct text checked.

sources.title: UNESCO: Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram
sources.note: Official property description and outstanding universal value. Seventh- and eighth-century Pallava monuments, monolithic rathas and structural Shore Temple. The page’s anomalous 638 to 660 dates for Rajasimha are not used. Direct page and indexed original checked.

sources.title: Edward Fosmire: The Great Relief at Mamallapuram, Smarthistory
sources.note: Art-historical account, 2019. Indexed original text checked; direct tool retrieval returned an internal error. Supports Kanchipuram and Mamallapuram, competing interpretations of the relief, elephants and calves, and the ascetic cat with mice. The cat is a depicted joke, not evidence of ordinary animal behavior or human household custom.

sources.title: National Museum, New Delhi: Somaskanda, accession 59.153/24
sources.note: Direct official catalogue checked. Buff granite, South India, Pallava, eighth century; Shiva and Parvati with Skanda on her lap, Brahma and Vishnu behind. The catalogue gives a region rather than a precise excavated findspot.

sources.title: Emmanuel Francis: Tiruvellarai great-well inscription, DHARMA INSPallava00098
sources.note: Indexed original edition and translation checked; direct retrieval failed. Construction begun in Dantivarman’s fourth regnal year and completed in his fifth; builder Kampan Araiyan and named well Marppituku-perunkinaru. The numbered corporate body guarding it is not treated as a population census. No exact calendar conversion asserted.

sources.title: V. Venkatasubba Ayyar: Kunnandarkoyil inscription, South Indian Inscriptions XII.46, DHARMA edition
sources.note: Direct transcription and editorial summary checked. Third year of Nandippottaraiyar, tentatively identified by the editor as Nandivarman III. Rice measured as 200 nali for feeding 100 people at Tiruvadirai; no conversion to modern volume units.

sources.title: H. Krishna Sastri: Tandantottam plates, South Indian Inscriptions II.99, DHARMA edition
sources.note: Direct original edition and translation checked. Nandivarman II, regnal year 58; calendar conversions differ, so described as late eighth century. Household permissions and exemptions in translation; Tamil lines 198 to 201 and 216 to 217 identify land shares for recitation, water and a physician. Same underlying charter as Karashima Table 3; the combined unique derived prose is separately budgeted.

sources.title: Noboru Karashima: Epigraphical Study of Ancient and Medieval Villages in the Tamil Country
sources.note: Direct scholarly research article checked, especially Table 3 and its introduction: Tandantottam charter of Nandivarman II. Physician two land shares, reciter one, drummer one, public-hall water supplier and water distributors. Table 4 concerns a thirteenth-century Pandya record and is not used.

sources.title: Emmanuel Francis: Uttiramerur, Nandivarman year 24, DHARMA INSPallava00078
sources.note: Direct revised edition based on autopsy and photographs, 2019. Translation lines 1 to 5 names three sellers including a Brahmin woman, food offerings funded from land, and tax exemption by the great assembly. Edition does not disambiguate the king in its title; no exact calendar date assigned. This is not the later Chola election inscription.

sources.title: Emmanuel Francis: Bahur plates of Nripatungavarman, year 8, DHARMA INSPallava00155
sources.note: Direct edition, Sanskrit and Tamil text and Hultzsch translation checked. Three villages assigned to a seat of learning; household and land categories in the grant; engraver and paternal ancestry named in verse 32 and Tamil lines 78 to 79. Ninth century. An unfinished translation has an isolated seventh-year discrepancy; title, Tamil text and older English translation support eighth year. No fourteen-subject curriculum claimed.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India: South Indian Inscriptions III, introduction, Aditya I
sources.note: Direct transcription of the ASI introduction checked, paragraphs on Aditya I. Tiruvalangadu plates report Aparajita’s defeat; Tirukkalukkunram inscription in Aditya’s 27th year ratifies an earlier Pallava grant. Precise conquest chronology is uncertain, so around 900 is used rather than an exact terminal year.

proposedOverrides.summary: Pallava rulers, stone monuments and village endowments in southern India.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Share one phased historical narrative; preserve both imported map intervals and associate both IDs explicitly.
batchIdentityNotes.basis: Consecutive labels in southern India, 500 to 800 then 800 to 1000; index and decoded feature bounds in identities.json. These describe the same Pallava continuity, not two unrelated dynasties. The final mapped century is beyond the main dynasty’s conquest around 900.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: Broad imported outlines are not a reconstruction of precise control. Early fourth-century evidence is background before the map window. No exact conquest year selected from competing modern chronologies. No blanket claim about universal schooling, sanitation, healthcare or women’s rights is made.
